words.gloss_range: definite divine proper name on an intensive mercy pattern; locally it names the source of mercy before any stated act, not a generic adjective or request for mercy
words.root_gloss_range: mercy, tenderness, pity, beneficence, kinship bond, and womb imagery are in the root range; the local proper name selects divine mercy while letting nurture and relational protection remain as narrowed pressure
words.prose: {{ar:ٱلرَّحْمَٰنُ}} ({{tr:al-raḥmānu}}) is a one-word nominal opening, so the name holds both a declaration and a forward pull: it can stand as a compressed identity statement, while the subject reading waits for the teaching predicate in 55:2. Its definiteness, nominative case, and proper-name shape prevent a generic adjective or object-role reading and fix the divine referent before the first action is heard. The intensive name-form makes mercy appear as an overflowing, abiding attribute rather than a timed act, petition, causative form, comparison, abstract noun, or counterpart epithet; it is a distributionally familiar proper-name choice from a broad mercy root. The root {{ar:ر ح م}} ({{tr:r-ḥ-m}}) supplies mercy, tenderness, sparing, and beneficent action; more narrowly, its womb and kinship branches lend nurture, enclosure, and protective relation without making physical wombs the local referent. Because the name is the whole ayah, structure and sound make it the complete opening beat: the joined definite onset, long central vowel, final nasal closure, and shared ending with the 55:2 object help the name carry the pause before later teaching, creation, calibration, and bounties unfold from it, including the surah-level return at 55:78 and wider authority contexts at 17:110, 19:45, and 20:5.

topics.headline: compressed identity and forward syntax
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the one-word ayah can feel complete as an identity declaration and still pull forward toward 55:2.
topics.reason: The bundle licenses the word as a nominative nominal utterance and marks predicate ellipsis as ambiguous, so both the elided-subject identity reading and the delayed-predicate subject reading survive, but neither should erase the other.

topics.headline: name governs later predicates
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that teaching, creation, calibration, and later bounty language are not loose follow-up statements but unfold under the opening name.
topics.reason: The CRITICAL rows present the initial nominal as a durable subject or frame for later predications, and the local syntax does not contradict that forward relation.

topics.headline: identity precedes action
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the discourse begins with who the act belongs to before any act is narrated.
topics.reason: The word is nominal rather than verbal, and the explicit name is retained before the next verbal predicate, so identity is grammatically foregrounded before event.

topics.headline: definite proper divine name
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the opening is not a generic mercy-quality but a known divine name with a fixed referent.
topics.reason: The word is tagged as a definite proper noun with dominant divine reference, and its nominative form keeps it in subject or predicate material rather than as the object of the following teaching verb.

topics.headline: intensive mercy-name morphology
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the form itself makes mercy feel full, inherent, and expansive before any recipient is named.
topics.reason: The QAC grammar identifies the intensive pattern, and the CRITICAL rows coherently contrast that selection with participial, finite-verbal, abstract-noun, and familiar counterpart options.

topics.headline: sourcehood over petition or derivation
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the root's mercy actions and requests are gathered into the named source of mercy, not staged as a seeker, recipient, comparison, or caused state.
topics.reason: The broader root family contains verbal, reciprocal, causative, comparative, passive-recipient, and request forms, but the local surface is a singular divine proper name, so those branches clarify contrast rather than become local predicates.

topics.headline: womb and kinship pressure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that mercy is colored by nurture, enclosure, and protective relation, while the local word remains a divine name rather than a physical-womb reference.
topics.reason: V4 accepts womb and kinship branches for the root, but the local NOUN_PROP divine-name form and referent profile require this material to remain narrowed root-image pressure, not the selected referent.

topics.headline: major name-form selected from a broad root
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah chooses a distributionally major proper-name form from a root that also offers abstract mercy, counterpart epithet, and concrete womb forms.
topics.reason: The contextual profiles confirm a high-count proper-name deployment with dominant divine reference, while the V4 branches preserve the wider root alternatives that the local form does not select.

topics.headline: standalone divine-name opener
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the entire opening slot is occupied by this name alone, without a verb, paired epithet, praise formula, oath, or letters sharing the first beat.
topics.reason: The ayah contains only the divine proper name as a nominal utterance, so the structural isolation is a real local feature rather than an imported thematic claim.

topics.headline: tight bridge to 55:2
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that 55:2 answers the opening name with the first displayed action under mercy: teaching.
topics.reason: The CRITICAL rows tie the one-word subject or declaration to the unconjoined teaching predicate in 55:2, making the boundary a semantic and syntactic bridge.

topics.headline: surah frame and authority echoes
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the name is not only local to 55:1; it frames the surah's later return at 55:78 and resonates with authority contexts at 17:110, 19:45, and 20:5.
topics.reason: The cited inter-ayah rows provide concrete references and a plausible formula contrast, while the topic is narrowed so those echoes support framing rather than control the local parse.

topics.headline: sound fills the one-word beat
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices how the single word is paced in recitation: a joined onset, a pressed opening consonant, a long central vowel, and final nasal closure carry the whole ayah.
topics.reason: The sound observations survive as recitational and structural payoff, but they are narrowed away from proving the semantics by themselves.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The isolated definite designation ٱلرَّحْمَٰنُ and its root ر ح م.
baseline_models.mechanism: The tenderness branch makes the one-word opening recipient-facing: mercy moves toward vulnerability as compassion and beneficence rather than remaining an abstract property.

activation_trace.role: Tenderness and beneficence supply the affective impulse and its outward movement toward one shown mercy.

changed_reading.before: A divine title conventionally glossed as the Merciful.
changed_reading.after: An abundant, recipient-facing movement of tenderness and beneficence, not an inert attribute.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The ر ح م root of ٱلرَّحْمَٰنُ can activate the kinship branch without leaving the focus word.
baseline_models.mechanism: Kinship turns mercy into a connective obligation: it makes giver and recipient non-strangers whose bond calls for maintenance rather than a one-off favor.

activation_trace.role: The close-kin bond supplies durable relation and the duty not to sever it.

changed_reading.before: Mercy is a benefactor's optional kindness to another.
changed_reading.after: Al-Rahman names the maker and keeper of a bond in which the recipient is treated as connected, not alien.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The ر ح م root of the focus name carries the womb branch.
baseline_models.mechanism: A womb is an enclosing, nourishing environment in which dependent life is formed. The name can therefore model mercy spatially and materially as a life-making surround.

activation_trace.role: The womb supplies enclosure, nourishment, dependence, and formation as a concrete mercy mechanism.

changed_reading.before: Mercy is primarily a feeling or favorable act.
changed_reading.after: Al-Rahman can name the containing ecology inside which fragile life becomes possible.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The focus root inventory preserves a branch of womb pain, disease, or retained afterbirth after delivery.
baseline_models.mechanism: The rare branch prevents the maternal image from becoming frictionless: generation leaves pain and residue that require continued care. Mercy may include repair after emergence, not only shelter before it.

activation_trace.role: Post-delivery womb affliction supplies vulnerability, residue, and the need for aftercare.

changed_reading.after: Al-Rahman may also evoke care that stays with the wound and unfinished aftermath of bringing forth.

context_deltas.mechanism: The opening sequence can be read as gestation: revelation is gathered and made knowable, its human recipient is brought into being, and interior meaning is delivered into signs. Mercy precedes the recipient and forms both the communicative world and the capacity to enter it.

activation_trace.role: The womb supplies the focus-anchored container and formation process.
The branch of a womb gathering a pregnancy makes the Quran's gathering function a gestational activator.
Disclosure to a knower supplies the movement from hidden content to apprehended knowledge.
Bringing creation into existence supplies formation of the receiving human.
Revealing meaning through speech or sign supplies the delivery of an interior into expression.

structural_cues: The isolated name is followed by three subjectless verbs whose implied actor is naturally carried forward from 55:1.
Teaching the Quran precedes creating the human, while teaching expression follows creation.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies gathering, disclosure, creation, expression, and their order; I supply the arrow that treats the order as a gestational process. A live alternative is a non-causal ranking of gifts.

changed_reading.before: The name announces kindness toward an already existing recipient.
changed_reading.after: Al-Rahman names a mercy that first prepares meaning, then forms its recipient, then brings the recipient into articulate response.

context_deltas.mechanism: Calculation, balance, equitable measure, assigned placement, and germinating seed turn mercy into an enabling order. Limits are not opposed to tenderness; proportion and non-transgression are the infrastructure by which a shared habitat remains fruitful.

activation_trace.role: Beneficence anchors the ordered system as recipient-serving rather than merely mechanical.
Counting and calculation supply predictable celestial measure.
The just balance makes proportion a moral as well as cosmic regulator.
Equity supplies the social distribution rule that preserves the shared order.
Putting something in its lower or assigned place turns earth into deliberately situated support.
The seed that germinates supplies the life-result made possible by measured placement.

structural_cues: 55:5-12 moves from calculated luminaries to a raised sky, a placed balance, commands against excess, earth for creatures, and reproductive food.
The same balance vocabulary joins cosmic description to human imperatives.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies calculation, balance, equity, placement, and growth; I infer that proportion causally enables flourishing and that social measure mirrors cosmic measure. Alternatively, balance may be a judicial demand adjacent to, rather than a mechanism of, mercy.

changed_reading.before: Mercy relaxes constraint and gives generously.
changed_reading.after: Al-Rahman is also the giver of exact limits whose fairness and stability let many lives flourish together.

context_deltas.mechanism: The recurring dual question converts gifts into claims on recognition, and it continues across warning scenes. structural_cues: The same dual refrain follows creation, provision, cosmic boundaries, mortality, threat, judgment, and gardens.

context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies the refrain's unchanged form across benefit and warning; I infer that warning can serve mercy by making limits answerable. context_deltas.mechanism: Early mercy teaches the outward sign of inward meaning; later, questioning falls away because persons are distinguishable by embodied marks and can be seized accordingly. context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies expression, absent questioning, recognition, marks, and taking; I infer one arc in which merciful communicability grounds answerability. A live alternative is that the early pedagogical and late judicial sign systems are unrelated.

changed_reading.after: Al-Rahman grants legibility itself: the power to express inward meaning and the condition of remaining readable to just consequence.

context_deltas.mechanism: Creaturely forms end, the divine face remains, dependents keep asking, and each bounded interval contains a fresh affair. Mercy shifts from guaranteeing permanent objects to continuously attending, repairing, and re-answering finite life.

context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies finitude, remaining, requests, daily duration, and affairs; I infer the request-to-renewed-maintenance arrow. A live alternative is a contrast of creaturely dependence with sovereignty, without implying temporal replenishment.

changed_reading.before: Mercy is possession of durable favorable things.

strongest_changes: The opening name became a gestational pedagogy that prepares meaning, forms a recipient, and delivers expression.
Mercy became calibrated habitat: balance and non-transgression are enabling conditions of flourishing.
The womb branch became a selective boundary that allows meeting and valuable emergence without collapse of difference.
Universal perishing revised mercy from permanent goods to continuously renewed care.
The recurring dual challenge made mercy an accountable address rather than exemption from consequence.
The final blessing of the Lord's name made the opening name a frame enacted by the whole surah.
summary.what_was_special: A one-word focus sustained several coexisting mechanisms instead of collapsing to a soft synonym: affective beneficence, kinship, womb ecology, calibrated order, selective concealment, communicative legibility, reciprocal relation, and severe boundary. The packet repeatedly made opposites productive: disclosure coexists with shelter, encounter with non-transgression, finitude with renewed care, and gift with accountability.
remaining_uncertainties: The childbirth, menstrual, and guarded-womb outliers depend on deliberately distant branches and should remain analogical rather than lexical.
The repeated refrain may place warnings within mercy's pedagogy, or may only place both gifts and warnings under lordship without calling the warnings merciful.
Protective opacity and judicial legibility may be sequential complements, or genuinely competing readings of what mercy does.
The shared dual address may constitute trans-kind kinship, or may simply coordinate two separate audiences.

reader_a.activated_readings_md:
1. **A title that initiates formation.** `ر ح م/B003` (womb) is activated by the verbless title followed by teaching, creating, and teaching (55:2–4). The packet gives the root branch and sequence; I infer that the title governs these acts as an enclosing source. The single word reads as compressed generative agency.
2. **Tenderness made operational.** `ر ح م/B001` assigns mercy the role of beneficence toward its recipient. Since the next clauses distribute recitation, existence, and articulation, I infer that mercy operates through capability-giving. The title reads less as an abstract epithet and more as the agentive premise of human formation.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: The judgment sequence (55:31–45) corrects a purely soft reading: mercy includes establishing limits, exposing denial, and making consequences visible. The later gardens then restore beneficence without erasing that correction.

reader_a.activated_readings_md: 1. **`ر ح م` `B001` and `B003` — “tender mercy” and “womb.”** Structural cue: the isolated nominal title is followed by three finite acts, teaching in 55:2 and 55:4 around human creation in 55:3. Assigned role: `B001` names the disposition behind the acts, while `B003` supplies their generative enclosure; these are coexisting images, not a merged branch. Packet evidence is the title-act sequence. Inference: the opening title governs the following verbs as their causal source. Reading change: “The Merciful” functions as the surah’s first explanatory premise.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: 55:5 unexpectedly broadened the title’s scope: ordered celestial reckoning suggests that the initiating mercy governs calibration beyond the human teaching-creation sequence.

facets.statement: Bir başkasının durumu karşısında yüreğin yumuşaması, ona acıma ve içten yakınlık duyma çekirdeği oluşturur.
Bu iç yöneliş, acınan kişiyi esirgemeyi ve ona iyilikte bulunmayı gerektiren etkin bir sonuç taşır.
Topluluğun bireylerinin birbirine acıyıp birbirini esirgemesi, çekirdeğin karşılıklı bir kuruluşta gerçekleşmesidir.
Bir kimsenin Tanrı'nın esirgemesine erişmesini dilemek, çekirdek anlamdan doğan kalıplaşmış bir söz eylemidir.
Tanrı hakkında kullanıldığında esirgemenin genişliği ve yaratılmışlara iyilik olarak ulaşması belirginleşir.

identity_judgment.rationale: Hazırlanan başlık doğumdan sonraki ağrıyı doğru bir merkez olarak gösterse de yetkili kaynak anlatımı bundan daha geniştir: dişi deve, koyun veya kadında döl yatağının ağrıması ya da hastalanması yanında şişme ve koyunun doğumdan sonra yavru zarını atamaması da aynı dalda yer alır. Dal bölünmeden korunabilir, fakat tanım yalnızca doğum sonrası ağrıyla sınırlandırılmamalıdır.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Dal sağlıklı organı veya genel beden ağrısını değil, döl yatağına özgü ağrı, hastalık, şişme ve doğum sonrası yavru zarını atamama durumlarını kapsar.

lexicalization_scope.note: Verilen biçimler döl yatağına özgü hastalık ve doğum sonrası bozuklukları bağımsız olarak adlandırır; tanım başka bir kalıptan yalın anlama aktarım yapmaz.

concept_map.definition: Dişi deve, koyun veya kadında döl yatağının ağrıması ya da hastalanmasıyla; koyunda ise ayrıca şişmesiyle belirlenen durumdur. Bazı kullanımlar bunu doğum sonrasına bağlar. Koyunun doğumdan sonra yavru zarını atamaması da bu organ çevresindeki özel bir bozukluk olarak dala dahildir.

facets.statement: Dişi hayvan veya kadında döl yatağının ağrıması ya da hastalanması temel durumdur; özellikle bazı kullanımlarda bu durum doğum sonrasında görülür.
Koyunun doğum yaptıktan sonra yavru zarını dışarı atamaması, dala bağlı özel bir doğum sonrası bozukluktur.
Koyun veya koyun sürüsünde döl yatağının şişmesi, hastalık durumunun özel bir gerçekleşmesidir.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Ortak anlatım, dişi deve, koyun veya kadının döl yatağında ağrı ya da hastalık bulunmasını temel alır. Kaynakların bir bölümü bunu özellikle doğum sonrasına bağlar. Toplu anlatım ayrıca koyunda organın şişmesini ve doğumdan sonra yavru zarının atılamamasını aynı organ çevresindeki özel durumlar olarak kaydeder.

Bedensel tarafta yavrunun geliştiği döl yatağı ve bu organa özgü ağrı, hastalık, şişme ya da doğum sonrası bozukluklar birbirinden ayrılır.

word_morpheme_spans.note: Accepted bridge links preserve independent analysis identities. Several analysis entries may share canonical morphemes. Read their distinct semantic claims; shared morphology alone is not duplication. Legacy aligned_qac_word_ref values are source observations, not QAC joins. Excluded source entries remain available with their explicit qualification.

word_analysis_qac_alignment.note: Legacy analysis and QAC numbers are separate source namespaces. Use accepted word_morpheme_spans for actual many-to-many joins. The legacy numbering observation is preserved, not used for alignment.

channel_review.note: first-pass blind review by a single reader; no adjudication, no accept/reject, no per-ayah channel maturity. Not a channel ledger.

channel_generated_outputs.note: Generated network-v3 channel discovery/family/path outputs are available as external quran-data files; read them only when channel detail is necessary, and do not treat them as an adjudicated channel ledger.

full_context_packet.note: surah-scope fallback: the default commentary workflow does not consume per-ayah focus packets, so the source packet is scoped by this builder to roots this ayah can justify and carries no staged reveal order

scoping.note: SCOPED, NOT ABSENT. The surah-scope fallback inventory covers every root in the surah; it is narrowed here to roots this ayah can justify -- roots occurring in this ayah (all their branches kept, unconditionally, because Layer 2 selects nothing) plus roots explicitly cited by channel material anchored here (only the cited branches kept, enough to resolve the citation). A root listed in dropped_roots is a deliberate scoping decision, not a missing source.

v12_reader_responses.note: Per-ayah focus-run reader responses are retired from the default commentary workflow. Use regular reader walks, plus/minus-5 reader walks, and cross-run publication findings for corpus-wide reader-derived evidence.

v12_cross_run_publication.note: Compact final cross-run findings for this ayah, reconciled upstream from regular and plus/minus-5 reader runs; use as a coverage/priority check, not as replacement prose.

occurrence_evidence_trim.note: TRIMMED, NOT ABSENT. dictionary_entry.occurrence_evidence.occurrences and .ayahs are removed from every root by design: they are a per-occurrence QAC concordance and character-span alignment table carrying zero readings, branches or senses, and they dominated bundle size (~1.5 MB for a single common root). occurrence_evidence.summary (corpus frequency) and .forms (inflectional inventory) are retained. Dictionary/gloss branches are kept in full for every included Furuq root target.

branch_policy.note: No branch filtering is applied. Every branch present in each included dictionary/gloss root entry is kept.

root_mapping.policy: Use the dominant Furuq root for every QAC root, and include non-dominant Furuq targets as additional root_lexicon entries when qac-furuq-v4-root-map marks the QAC root as split.
